subject: Chemistry
description: Molarity, molality, normality, saturated vs unsaturated, colligative properties

options.option_text: Homogeneous mixture of two or more substances

questions.explanation: Solution — homogeneous mixture (uniform composition throughout). Components: SOLUTE (lesser amount, dissolved) + SOLVENT (larger, dissolves). Example: salt in water — salt is solute, water is solvent. Air = mixture of gases (N₂, O₂, etc.) — also a solution.
questions.subject: Chemistry

options.option_text: Moles of solute per kg of solvent
Moles of solute per litre of solution

questions.explanation: Molarity (M) = moles of solute / litre of SOLUTION. Molality (m) = moles of solute / kg of SOLVENT. Normality = g-equivalents / L. Molality doesn't change with temperature (solvent mass is fixed); molarity does (volume changes).
questions.subject: Chemistry

options.option_text: Cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature
Always holds the maximum possible at any temperature

questions.explanation: Saturated — contains the maximum solute that can dissolve at a given temperature; equilibrium with solid. Unsaturated — can dissolve more. Supersaturated — metastable, contains more than the saturation limit; often unstable (crystallises out on small disturbance).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: When common salt is added to water, the BOILING POINT of the solution:
questions.explanation: Colligative property: dissolving a non-volatile solute RAISES the boiling point and LOWERS the freezing point. Used to de-ice roads (salt on ice). Salt in cooking water makes water boil slightly above 100 °C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: M(H₂O) = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. Useful reference. 18 g = 1 mole = 6.022 × 10²³ molecules. 18 mL ≈ 18 g (density ~1 g/mL for water) ≈ 1 mole.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Avogadro's number = 6.022 × 10²³ per mole — number of particles in 1 mole. 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C = elementary charge (electron). 9.8 m/s² = standard g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: A 10% (w/w) aqueous solution of salt means:

options.option_text: 10 g of salt in 100 g of water
10 g of salt in 100 g of SOLUTION
10 mL of salt in 100 mL water

questions.explanation: w/w — weight of solute per weight of total solution. 10 g salt in 100 g solution (= 10 g salt + 90 g water). Similar: w/v (mass/volume), v/v (volume/volume), ppm (mg/kg or mg/L for dilute aqueous).
